subject: dyamic specification of variable name into ggvis/dplyr construction

messages.author: 3b0940ce7a895cd1
messages.subject: dyamic specification of variable name into ggvis/dplyr construction
parts:
I am trying to reactively change the sort order specification for a ggvis plot within a shiny reactive document. More broadly I am trying to force dynamic variable name selection into a ggvis specification, but ...


The static code:

library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

diamonds%>%
  group_by(color)%>%
  ggvis(x=~carat, y=~price)%>%
  layer_points(fill=~color)%>%
  layer_smooths(stroke=~color)

produces the expected plot.


As a next step towards making the graph reactive, I wanted to make the stratifying variable ("color" in the above example) reactive:

---
title: "Untitled"
runtime: shiny
output: html_document
---

## Inputs and Outputs

```{r}
#library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)
data(diamonds)

```{r}

inputPanel(
 
selectInput(inputId = "varchoice", choices = names(diamonds), selected = "price", label = "Variable Choice")
 
)
 
renderPlot({
        
diamonds%>%
  group_by(input$varchoice)%>%
  ggvis(x=~carat, y=~price)%>%
  layer_points(fill=input$varchoice)%>%
  layer_smooths(stroke=input$varchoice)

})
```
This is the end.

The selectInput function is working as expected and produces the input box with all of the variable names from diamonds, but I then see the error: object 'input' not found .

I have tried several other variations, including casting the input$varchoice inside the as.name function, but none of my efforts have been successful in moving the value input$varchoice into the graph specification in a way that is synatically correct.
  
I would welcome suggestions on how to dynamically change this variable.

I am optimistic that once I can change the sort order/fill/stroke variable, I will also have the insight to be able to change the X axis variable, but ... one problem at a time.

Regards,



Thanks,

messages.author: 32b56b82e6afcfce
messages.subject: Re: dyamic specification of variable name into ggvis/dplyr construction
parts:
Hello Rob,
I am wondering if you were every able to come up with a solution to using the group_by function with an input string inside it.  I am attempting to make a ggvis plot using variable name inputs and would like to add a regression option.  I have been unable to use the group_by function within my application.  Depending on what I put inside the group_by(), I get an error saying "Error: is.broker(input) is not TRUE" or "Error: index out of bounds." Please see sample code below.  Any ideas would be greatly appreciated.  Thanks!
-Jesse

xvar <- input$x
yvar <- input$y
colorvar <- input$color
shapevar <- input$shape
sizevar <- input$size

xc <- prop ("x", as.symbol (xvar))
yc <- prop("y", as.symbol(yvar))
fillc <- prop("fill", as.symbol(colorvar))
shapec <- prop("shape", as.symbol(shapevar))
sizec <- prop ("size", as.symbol (sizevar))

df %>% ggvis(x=xc, y=yc) %>% 
layer_points(fill= fillc, shape= shapec, size=sizec) %>%
group_by(as.name(eval(colorvar))) %>%
layer_model_predictions(model = "lm")

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: dyamic specification of variable name into ggvis/dplyr construction
parts:
Hi Jesse,

There is now a standard-evaluation version of "group_by", called "group_by_". Would a formulation like this work for you?

df %>% ggvis(x=xc, y=yc) %>% 
layer_points(fill= fillc, shape= shapec, size=sizec) %>%

group_by_(colorvar) %>%
layer_model_predictions(model = "lm")

I'm still a bit wobbly on the whole standard/non-standard evaluation thing, but it might be a place to start.

Ian
